The Court made the following:
 THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE VENKATESWARLU NIMMAGADDA  WRIT PETITION NO: 10932/2025 ORDER:
This writ petition is filed under Article 226 of the Constitution of the India seeking the following reliefs:-
to issue a writ, order or direction more particularly one in the nature of Writ of Mandamus declaring the action of the 3'"^ respondent in not passing the award in respect of the land to an extent of Ac.1.45 cents covered by Sy.No.30 to 38 of VIruvuru Village, Podalakuru Mandal, SPSR Nellore District and not paying the compensation amount to the petitioners as illegal, arbitrary and in violation of Article 300- B Suresh Kumar Reddy vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 6 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/60432589/
3 A of Constitution of India and conseguently direct the respondents to pass award and pay the compensation as per the provisions of Act 30 of 2013 to the petitioners in respect of the land to an extent of Ac. 1.45 cents covered by Sy.No.30 to 38 of Viruvuru Village, Podalakuru Mandal, SPSR Nellore District and pass such other order. "

2. Though the petitioners made several allegations against the respondents, during hearing, learned counsel for the petitioners requested this Court, to issue a direction to the respondents to dispose of the representation dated 18.06.2024 filed by the petitioners.

3. Learned Assistant Government Pleader for the respondents furnished written instructions issued by the 3 respondent dated 25.04.2025, wherein it is stated as follows:
"The then LAO & RDO, Nellore Initiated LA proceedings under Act 30 of 2013 and preliminary notifications and declarations notified In the manner prescribed under the Act.
The objections filed by the villagers also rejected vide Rc.B(LA).3369/2017, dated 23.11.2022, market value also fixed duly following procedure under Section 26(1)(a)(b)(c)(2) of Act 30 of 2013.

Award enquiry also conducted. "
4.
In view of the written instructions furnished by the learned Assistant Government Pleader for Revenue, this Court need not decide the truth or otherwise of the allegations made in the petition.

This Court is conscious that no such direction be issued, in view of the judgment of the Apex Court in "The Government of India v. P.Venkatesh^", wherein the Apex Court held that such orders may make for a quick or easy disposal of cases in overburdened adjudicatory institutions.
But, they do not serve to the cause of justice.

As the learned counsel for the petitioners himself requested to issue a direction to dispose of the representation dated 18.06.2024, this Court find no other alternative except to issue such direction.

5. In the result, the writ petition is disposed of, directing the respondents to consider and dispose of the representation dated 18.06.2024 filed by the petitioners, within a period of three (3) months from the date of receipt of a copy of this order.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Cv As a sequel miscellaneous application, pending, if any, shall also stand closed.
